title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get — and in cyclical capital-intensive franchises, the multiple at the trough of earnings always looks highest right before operating leverage takes over.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: At $303.60 per share (as of November 13, 2026), Texas Instruments holds a $277.42B market cap and a $282.83B enterprise value on 914.00M diluted shares.[2][12] On trailing 12-month (TTM) metrics, TXN trades at 39.39x P/E ($7.71 TTM EPS) and 37.91x P/FCF. It also trades at 26.19x EV/EBITDA, 13.62x EV/Sales ($20.77B TTM revenue), and 14.46x P/B.[12] Its trailing dividend yield is 1.90% ($5.78/sh TTM, or $6.08 annualized at the $1.52 quarterly rate).[9][12] On forward estimates, the multiple drops to 26.06x Forward P/E (~$11.65 forward EPS) with a 0.73x PEG ratio (35.87% projected 5-year EPS CAGR).[12] That 13.3-turn gap between trailing and forward P/E defines the debate. The market already prices in much of the 2026–2027 margin rebound, leaving thin room for error at $303.60.

A Reverse DCF at $282.83B EV shows what $303.60 demands. We use an 8.5% WACC, reflecting TXN's A+/Aa3 balance sheet, 1.39 beta, and 33% industrial / 33% auto mix. With a 3.5% terminal growth rate, TXN must generate $17.5B–$19.0B in annual unlevered FCF by Year 10. That starts from a normalized $6.5B–$7.0B base, stripping one-time 2026 CHIPS grants out of $8.42B TTM FCF.[2][5] That path requires a 10.5%–11.5% 10-year FCF CAGR. To hit it, sales must grow ~6.5%–7.5% a year toward ~$38B–$42B by 2036, aided by Silicon Labs. FCF margin must also rise from ~31%–34% today toward 45%–48% as capex stays at $2B–$3B and 300mm fabs top 80% load.[4] At $303.60, TXN is neither cheap nor a bubble. It assumes Haviv Ilan's 2026–2030 FCF ramp lands smoothly without a new industrial slump.

Reverse DCF FCF-Margin Bridge & Bear Sensitivity: Why does $303.60 assume a 45%–48% steady-state FCF margin when TXN peaked at 34.3% in FY2021 and 29.6% in FY2022?[7] In FY2021–FY2022, CapEx ran at 13.4%–14.0% of revenue and 300mm wafer mix was lower.[4][7] Stepping CapEx down to ~6.4% of $39.0B Year-10 revenue ($2.5B) plus higher 300mm gross margins adds ~1,100–1,300 bps to FCF margin.[4] Even so, that bridge carries real downside risk. Reverting Year-10 FCF margin to 34.3% on $39.0B revenue yields $13.38B FCF (0.7332x of the $18.25B midpoint). That scales implied EV to $207.37B and equity value to ~$220.96/sh (-27.2% below $303.60 CMP), matching our $225.00 Bear case. Rising Treasury yields reinforce that valuation cap: US10Y sits at 5.10% (+20 bps WoW) and US2Y sits at 4.86% (+28 bps WoW).[15]

web_blocks.takeaway: At $303.60, TXN trades right on its historical mid-cycle quality multiple (26.06x forward P/E) while discounting ~11% annualized FCF compounding over the next decade. New capital needs a pullback to $278–$286 to build a wider margin of safety.

web_blocks.html: TXN's 10-year valuation bands show why entry price matters. From 2016 to 2025, TXN traded at 18x to 28x forward earnings in normal expansions. It topped 35x–40x only during trough earnings, as in 2023–2025 when capex and low fab loads depressed EPS.[7][12] Dividend yield also tracks the cycle well. Yields above 2.8%–3.2% marked prime buy zones in 2018, 2020, and late 2023. Yields below 2.0% signaled full near-term expectations. At a 1.90% trailing yield ($5.78 TTM; 2.00% on the $6.08 forward rate), TXN sits at the rich end of its yield band despite 23 straight dividend hikes.[9][12] Its 13.62x EV/Sales also tops its pre-2020 7x–9x range. That multiple holds only if operating margins stay above 41% and FCF margins top 40%.

web_blocks.takeaway: TXN's 22.04% ROIC is more than double ADI's 10.25% (compressed by Maxim acquisition goodwill) and 50% above NXPI's 14.63%, justifying a quality premium—yet ADI trades at a slightly lower Forward P/E (23.65x vs 26.06x) with faster Q/Q sales growth (+39.63% vs +27.69%).

web_blocks.html: The peer table shows a clear two-tier split in analog chips. Tier-1 leaders (TXN and ADI) trade at 13.6x–14.4x EV/Sales and 23.7x–26.1x Forward P/E. Both hold >60% gross margins and strong industrial pricing power. TXN leads every peer with 22.04% ROIC and 41.12% operating margin. ADI posts 10.25% ROIC due to Maxim goodwill, while NXPI sits at 14.63%.[12][18][19] Meanwhile, Tier-2 peers (NXPI, MCHP, ON, STM) trade at 14.0x–17.0x Forward P/E and 2.9x–6.9x EV/Sales. They face heavier EV/SiC price pressure, weak European auto sales, and lower fab loads.[20][21][22] Value buyers may eye NXPI at 14.44x Forward P/E and 19.21x P/FCF. Still, TXN's 300mm cost edge and direct sales justify its Tier-1 multiple.

The $7.5B all-cash Silicon Labs deal (announced February 4, 2026; closing H1 2027) adds a modest leverage overlay.[6] TXN ended Q3 2026 with $8.14B in cash ($8.91/sh) and $13.65B in gross debt (0.71x Debt/Equity, 5.59x Current Ratio).[2][12] Paying $7.5B in cash—likely using cash on hand plus ~$4B–$5B of new bonds—lifts net debt from ~$5.5B to ~$12B–$13B. That equals 1.1x–1.3x pro-forma EBITDA, which stays conservative. Even so, it slows share buybacks until 2028. Management must also deliver the targeted $450M in annual synergies by moving Silicon Labs wafers into TXN's 300mm fabs.[6]

Sensitivity of Fair Value to WACC & Terminal Margin: Flexing WACC by +/-50 bps (8.0%–9.0%) and steady-state FCF margin by +/-200 bps (44%–48%) gives an intrinsic value of $275 to $345 per share. That puts $303.60 right in the middle of fair value. Notice how closely this maps to our chart levels. The $278–$286 zone prices TXN at ~23.8x–24.5x forward EPS for a 22% ROIC leader. Our $345 Base target marks full fair value (1.00:1 from CMP, 2.46:1 from $286 support).

Why Capital-Cycle Timing Distorts Trailing Multiples: Quantitative screens often reject TXN for its 39.39x trailing P/E and 37.91x P/FCF.[12] That view misses the fab utilization bridge. Trailing results still carry heavy startup depreciation from new 300mm fabs (RFAB2 and SM1), which depresses trailing EPS ($7.71). Consensus forward EPS (~$11.65, or 26.06x Forward P/E) already assumes 62%–64% gross margins and $2B–$3B capex.[2][4][12] At $303.60, the recovery is priced in, making $278.00–$286.00 the right buy zone.

Valuation Bridge to 2028E–2030E: Suppose TXN reaches ~$25B–$27B in revenue by 2028–2029 with a full year of Silicon Labs. At 45%+ operating margins and $2.5B annual capex, normalized FCF can top $9.5B–$11.0B (~$10.40–$12.00 per share). Applying a 28x–30x quality multiple to $11.50+ FCF/share supports our $345.00 Base target and $390.00 Bull target over 12 to 24 months.[4][6][12]

Valuation Trigger: We turn buyers of new TXN shares only on a pullback into $278.00–$286.00 (~23.8x–24.5x Forward P/E), or if forward EPS estimates revise above $13.00 on faster 300mm fab loading. Conversely, a drop in gross margin below 60% or an unhedged Silicon Labs cost overrun cuts our Base fair value below $290.00.

web_blocks.title: Valuation Takeaway: Quality Is Priced In at $303.60; Margin of Safety Awaits at $278–$286
paragraphs: TXN at $303.60 (26.06x Forward P/E, 26.19x EV/EBITDA, 1.90% yield) fairly prices the 2026 FCF rebound. Its 22.04% ROIC and 41.12% operating margin lead all peers. Even so, the stock gives zero valuation cushion if industrial demand pauses or Silicon Labs hits snags.

book_paragraphs: At $303.60 per share as of November 13, 2026, Texas Instruments commands a market capitalization of $277.42 billion and an enterprise value of $282.83 billion. On trailing twelve-month results, the headline multiples look demanding: 39.39 times trailing earnings ($7.71 EPS), 37.91 times free cash flow, 26.19 times EV/EBITDA, 13.62 times EV/Sales ($20.77 billion TTM revenue), and 14.46 times book value, alongside a 1.90% trailing dividend yield ($5.78 per share TTM, or $6.08 annualized following the September 2026 dividend hike to $1.52 quarterly). Yet looking solely at trailing numbers misses the cyclical inflection already underway. On forward consensus estimates, the P/E ratio compresses by more than 13 turns to 26.06 times, with a 0.73x PEG ratio anchored by 35.87% projected five-year EPS growth.

That 13-turn gap between trailing and forward earnings is the core tension in TXN's valuation. After two years of industrial and automotive inventory digestion and peak 300mm wafer fab construction, the market has already repriced TXN up 86.80% over the past twelve months—from a 52-week low of $152.73 to a high of $334.03—anticipating the margin and cash-flow recovery.

To test what $303.60 actually requires from the business, we run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow model at the $282.83 billion enterprise value. Using an 8.5% weighted average cost of capital—appropriate for an A+-rated balance sheet with a 1.39 beta and industrial cyclicality—and a 3.5% terminal growth rate, the current enterprise value implies that TXN must generate roughly $17.5 billion to $19.0 billion in annual unlevered free cash flow by Year 10. Measured against a normalized post-capex-peak baseline of $6.5 billion to $7.0 billion (stripping out one-time 2026 CHIPS Act timing inflows from the $8.42 billion TTM FCF print), that requires a 10.5% to 11.5% ten-year FCF CAGR.

Is an 11% ten-year FCF CAGR realistic? Yes, if two things happen together. First, revenue must compound at 6.5% to 7.5% annually, growing from $20.77 billion today toward $38 billion to $42 billion by 2036, aided by Silicon Labs' IoT wireless portfolio and secular content growth in industrial automation, EVs, and data-center power. Second, free cash flow margins must expand from the low-30% range toward 45% to 48% as capital expenditures step down from $4.55 billion–$5.07 billion into management's $2 billion–$3 billion steady-state framework and 300mm fabs reach high utilization. In other words, $303.60 is neither cheap nor irrational; it simply leaves little margin of safety if the recovery stalls.

To test that 45% to 48% steady-state margin assumption, compare it with TXN's FY2021 and FY2022 peaks of 34.3% and 29.6%. Back then, CapEx ran at 13.4% to 14.0% of revenue and 300mm wafer share was lower. Dropping Year-10 CapEx to ~$2.5 billion (~6.4% of $39.0 billion revenue) alongside higher 300mm gross margins adds 1,100 to 1,300 basis points to FCF margin. Yet if Year-10 FCF margin reverts to 34.3% on $39.0 billion revenue, FCF falls to $13.38 billion (0.7332x of the $18.25 billion midpoint). That scales implied enterprise value to $207.37 billion and equity value to ~$220.96 per share—27.2% below $303.60 CMP. Meanwhile, higher Treasury yields act as a macro rate headwind: US10Y stands at 5.10% (+20 bps WoW) and US2Y sits at 4.86% (+28 bps WoW), limiting multiple expansion.

book_subsections.title: Historical Bands, Peer Comps & The Silicon Labs Balance Sheet Check
paragraphs: TXN's 10-year valuation history tells a similar story of fair-to-full pricing. Over the past decade, TXN has typically traded between 18 times and 28 times forward earnings during normal economic expansions, while its dividend yield has acted as a reliable cycle gauge. Historically, yields above 2.8% to 3.2% signaled deep cyclical troughs and attractive long-term entry points, whereas yields below 2.0% marked periods where near-term expectations ran ahead of fundamentals. At 1.90% trailing yield (2.00% on the new $6.08 annualized payout), TXN sits at the tighter end of its historical yield range despite 23 consecutive years of dividend increases.

Comparing TXN against its five closest analog and power-semiconductor peers—Analog Devices (ADI), NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), Microchip Technology (MCHP), ON Semiconductor (ON), and STMicroelectronics (STM)—highlights a sharp bifurcation. TXN ($277.42 billion market cap) and ADI ($192.84 billion) form the Tier-1 quality cohort, both commanding >60% gross margins (60.24% for TXN, 60.39% for ADI) and 13.6x–14.4x EV/Sales. TXN stands alone on capital efficiency, however: its 22.04% ROIC and 41.12% operating margin are more than double ADI's 10.25% ROIC (diluted by Maxim acquisition goodwill) and 50% higher than NXPI's 14.63% ROIC. Meanwhile, Tier-2 peers NXPI, MCHP, ON, and STM trade at 14.0x to 17.0x Forward P/E and 2.9x to 6.9x EV/Sales, reflecting heavier exposure to EV/SiC pricing pressure and European auto weakness.

To appreciate why that valuation gap exists, look closely at the cash-conversion and margin spread across the peer group. ON Semiconductor generates 38.13% gross margins and 6.02% ROIC; STMicroelectronics generates 35.36% gross margins and 2.51% ROIC; Microchip sits at 51.33% gross margins and 6.89% ROIC. Even NXP, which runs a disciplined 55.68% gross margin and 29.92% operating margin, cannot match TXN's 41.12% operating margin or 22.04% ROIC. Only ADI rivals TXN on gross margin (60.39% vs. 60.24%), and ADI currently trades at 23.65x Forward P/E and 28.71x EV/EBITDA—slightly cheaper than TXN on Forward P/E and slightly richer on EV/EBITDA—while delivering faster Q/Q revenue growth (+39.63% vs. +27.69%). That comparison tells us TXN's 26.06x forward multiple is earned, not irrational, yet leaves no room for disappointment.

Finally, investors must factor in the $7.5 billion all-cash Silicon Labs acquisition announced in February 2026 and slated to close in the first half of 2027. TXN enters the transaction from a position of strength, holding $8.14 billion in cash and short-term investments against $13.65 billion in gross debt (0.71x debt-to-equity and a 5.59x current ratio). Even if TXN funds the deal with a mix of cash on hand and $4 billion to $5 billion of new debt, pro-forma net leverage will settle around 1.1x to 1.3x EBITDA—easily manageable for a business generating >$10 billion in EBITDA, though it will temporarily curtail discretionary share buybacks until 2028 while management executes on $450 million in targeted 300mm manufacturing and operating synergies.

Put all three valuation lenses together—the Reverse DCF requiring ~11% ten-year FCF compounding, the 1.90% dividend yield sitting near the richer end of TXN's 10-year historical band, and the Tier-1 peer comparison against ADI and NXPI—and a clear conclusion emerges. At $303.60, TXN is fairly priced for a smooth 2027–2028 recovery. Waiting for a pullback into the $278.00 to $286.00 support zone lowers the forward multiple toward ~23.8x–24.5x, lifts the annualized dividend yield toward ~2.13%–2.19%, and restores an institutional margin of safety.

Let us also test our DCF assumptions for sensitivity so you can see where the valuation floor actually sits. If we flex the weighted average cost of capital by 50 basis points in either direction—between 8.0% and 9.0%—and flex steady-state free cash flow margins between 44% and 48%, our intrinsic value grid spans roughly $275 to $345 per share. Notice how neatly that fundamental range maps onto the technical chart: $278 to $286 sits right at the lower bound of fair value, while $345 represents our Base Case twelve-month target.

Finally, remember why quantitative stock screeners often misread Texas Instruments at this exact point in the cycle. On trailing twelve-month numbers, a 39.39x P/E and 37.91x P/FCF look expensive next to NXPI at 20.84x P/E and 19.21x P/FCF. Yet TXN's trailing earnings still carry the startup depreciation of newly opened 300mm fabs, whereas forward consensus (~$11.65 EPS, or 26.06x Forward P/E) already gives TXN credit for the 2026 margin rebound. That is why paying $303.60 leaves no cushion—while buying support at $278 to $286 captures a 22.04% ROIC compounder at a fair mid-cycle multiple.

Looking out toward 2028 and 2029, the earnings bridge becomes even clearer. If TXN scales revenue to $25 billion to $27 billion with a full year of Silicon Labs contribution, holds gross margins in the 62% to 64% range, and keeps capital expenditures near $2.5 billion annually, normalized free cash flow can reach $9.5 billion to $11.0 billion, or roughly $10.40 to $12.00 per share. Putting a standard 28x to 30x Tier-1 compounder multiple on $11.50 of free cash flow per share naturally supports our $345.00 Base target—and $390.00 in a stronger industrial upcycle.

book_callouts.title: Why 26x Forward P/E Needs a Pullback Entry
book_callouts.text: TXN's 22.04% ROIC and 60.24% gross margin justify a Tier-1 multiple, but at $303.60 the market is already pricing in a smooth 2027 FCF bridge. Waiting for $278–$286 aligns valuation discipline with technical support.
